articleTitle: Tape recording of mine shaft signals
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The recording of bell signals is not new. It was done on the Karlick tachograph by means of inking pens. Then magnetic recording was tried some years ago but wire was used as the recording medium and this was too bulky for satisfactory storage. The inking pens were re-introduced some years later and records are still being made on a narrow paper tape. Experiments were then carried out with a magnetic tape recorder to find out if it was feasible to use this type of recorder—and to find out some of the difficulties.

articleTitle: Vote of thanks
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: G. R. Bozzoli (Past President): The Institute has frequently been privileged in having eminent engineers from other countries to deliver papers before its members and the Institute has also, from time to time, had papers read which have been supported by demonstrations. It is safe to say, however, that never before have we been fortunate enough to experience both an eminent overseas engineer and a spectacular presentation of experiments at one and the same time. The occasion is all the more noteworthy because the demonstration equipment was practically all brought specially from England for tonight's exhibition.

articleTitle: The provision of standby power supplies for carrier telephone equipment
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The general problem of the provision of standby power supply for telephone carrier-frequency equipment operating directly from public alternating-current supplies is considered. The methods of providing such a supply are discussed and some of the problems which have been encountered in the practical application of these methods are detailed.

articleTitle: A method of calculating overhead transmission line sags for broken conductor conditions
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The author wishes to thank those who contributed to the discussion on the broken-conductor problem at road crossings by overhead transmission lines. The deficiencies in his method of arriving at the sag under broken conductor condition are fully appreciated and were, in fact, detailed fairly fully in the paper. It is maintained, however, that the formula described gives a quick and ready means of checking whether sufficient clearance is obtained provided the user is aware of its limitations. It should not be overlooked that calculations of this nature are usually made for the maximum designed working temperature of the conductor whereas, it may be reasonably assumed, the line will trip out on a break occurring and the resulting cooling off of the conductor will cause it to lift by an amount which in most cases more than compensates for the optimistic result obtained with the formula.

articleTitle: Design and operating experience with large Turbo-type A.C. generators
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: AUTHOR'S REPLY TO DISCUSSION Replying to Mr C. Ryder, generators controlled by the latest type of automatic voltage regulator, which has no ‘dead band’ and a high speed of response to voltage, load, and power-factor changes, can be operated much closer to the stability limit than is possible when they are controlled by the older vibrating contact type regulators. This should make it possible to use generators with lower short-circuit ratios than were previously required to deal with leading load conditions.

articleTitle: Standard frequency and time signal transmissions from the union observatory, Johannesburg
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Deviations of frequencies and time signals are with respect to the weighted mean of six quartz oscillators, and time signals from WWV over 20-day intervals. A positive frequency deviation indicates that the frequency is high. A time deviation of 010 indicates that the time pulses were 0.010 second late on WWV while 990 indicates that they were 0.010 second early. A value of 46.3 milliseconds has been adopted for the propagation time of radio signals between Washington and Johannesburg.

articleTitle: Specialised electrical auxiliary equipment for shaft sinking
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: There is a number of aspects of mining practice where there is scope for papers reviewing present-day practices. From the electrical point of view in particular very little has been done to record these developments. Possibly this is due to the fact that electrical equipment, though vital, tends to be rather unobtrusive—particularly in the case of control and interlocking circuits or safety devices which come into operation only when something goes wrong.

articleTitle: Some problems concerning the design of large power transformers
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The situation with regard to the consumption of electric power for a long time has been an increase of 5 to 10 per cent per year in all industrialized countries and there is no evidence whatsoever that this picture should change in the near future. This exponential increase has in the last years reached such magnitude that practical solutions can hardly be obtained by adopting the methods of yesterday but require radical changes in technique to transmit large amounts of electric power. This requirement concentrates especially on the high-voltage lines and on the power transformers as being the keys to the amount of power which it is possible to transmit from technical as well as economical points of view.

articleTitle: The balanced unsymmetrical parallel-T network as a three-terminal frequency-dependent bridge for the measurement of capacitance and dissipation factor
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The application of the balanced un-symmetrical parallel-T network as a frequency-dependent three-terminal bridge for the measurement of capacitance and dissipation-factor is analysed and the theory of operation and design procedure are explained in considerable detail. It is shown that the bridge is particularly suited to the accurate direct measurement of large capacitors of substantial dissipation factors at low frequencies, a measurement which has posed considerable difficulty in the past. It is shown that the unknown dissipation factor enters in a difference expression into the equation for the unknown capacitance and lot, as in most four-terminal bridges in common use, in the form of a product — the capacitance of a relatively lossy capacitor is thus obtained more accurately in this form of bridge.

articleTitle: Silicon as a material for power rectifiers
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Since the first copper oxide rectifiers were commercially produced in 1925, semiconductor rectifiers have become increasingly important for power rectification. Copper oxide, selenium and germanium rectifiers have been well known for many years. Recently, a new power rectifier has been developed — the silicon rectifier — which appears very promising for many applications, especially when it is essential to operate at ambient temperatures above 100°C. The purpose of this lecture is to describe the preparation of the basic material from which these rectifiers are made, and their mode of operation and manufacture. Firstly, a brief description will be given of the electrical properties of the basic material.

articleTitle: Light current section — chairman's address: Telegraph switching systems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper deals with the modern methods of switching of telegraph messages rather than the general principles of telegraphy which are well known and have developed somewhat slowly, although there are indications that we are on the eve of dramatic changes.

articleTitle: Electricity in the production of oil
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper is mainly descriptive. It deals in general terms with some of the many ways in which electricity enters into the production of crude oil from a particular oilfield and into the transport of this oil by pipeline to the coast. Orthodox plant is described briefly in order to devote more space to less commonly used equipment. Some mention is made of operating experiences.

articleTitle: Airport lighting
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Airport lighting is a very specialized art which involves a great many problems that do not occur in most other fields of electrical illumination. Present-day systems have gradually evolved from work carried out during the past 30 years in many different countries of the world.

articleTitle: A critical review of present trends in low- and medium-voltage cables
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: It is only when a particular type of equipment starts giving excessive trouble that its importance to the community becomes apparent. Nowhere is this more obvious than in the case of electric cables — normally taken for granted by the average engineer and quite certainly to be buried and forgotten. However, when cables start failing in the early hours of the morning, disrupt important services and disturb the peace of the supply authority, then their importance is appreciated. We, in South Africa, had this brought home to us in no uncertain manner when there was an epidemic of troubles, experienced on 11-kV cables in particular, which gave rise to many learned dissertations and theories propounded in club, committee and consulting rooms and a loss of sleep to many engineers. Catch words and phrases such as ‘surges,’ ‘altitude derating,’ ‘aspiration,’ ‘inferior cable manufacture’ and ‘careless installation and workmanship’ became the order of the day.

articleTitle: Electronic principles of the Tellurometer
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: An operational description of the Tellurometer system of distance measurement has been published but gives only the minimum of electronic detail for a broad understanding of the system. This paper is intended to supplement the operational description and will be confined to the electronic aspects only.

articleTitle: Electrical engineering—A century of progress
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: When I heard that next year this Institute is to celebrate fifty years of existence, during which it has grown to more than ten times its original size, and knowing that it would not be possible for me to be with you on that occasion, although I very much hoped at one time that that would be possible, it seemed to me not inappropriate that we might devote our time this evening to a consideration of the past one hundred years, during which the remarkable electrical technology which we know today started from quite simple beginnings. Therefore, Mr President, with your permission, that is the theme of my talk tonight.

articleTitle: A review of the post office telecommunication system in South Africa
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In choosing a subject for this address, it seemed desirable that I should be guided by custom and follow in some respects the general pattern of the addresses presented by the late Mr C. Griffith in 1938 and Mr J. A. F. Michell in 1950 and to extend and bring up to date some of the data given by them.

articleTitle: The conceivable future of telecommunications
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: When I was invited to come to South Africa and deliver this memorial lecture, my immediate sensations were those of pleasure and of a feeling of the great honour which had been done me, mingled however with surprise that I should have been selected by your Council for this undertaking. For this is the first time that I have visited this country, so that I come as a stranger; my only previous contacts with you have been the slender one of scientific correspondence and more intimate ones through South African students who occasionally have come to work with me in London. This situation is now remedied.

articleTitle: The maintenance of telecommunication plant with special reference to South Africa
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper reviews briefly the problem of maintaining telecommunication plant. It deals with the basic causes of faults, the various philosophies of maintenance, the effects of developments in the design of exchange and transmission equipment, the design of fault recording and analysis systems and the organization and staffing of maintenance work. The conclusion is reached that the dynamic and self-regulating policy of ‘qualitative’ maintenance increases service quality while substantially reducing costs.
